title: Her vents, 1912: the ways each space's air can leave her, for NH7 (in R3's form)
written: 2026-11-23, about 20:00 CST, by NH2's side session of the coordinator, at its word of 19:27, for Z1's NH7 design (docs/DESIGN_NH7_air_in_every_space_v1_2026-11-23.md, on claude/z1-z6-onset 5dcca8d); the machinery's rows with B1+B2's reading of The Shipbuilder (1911) and of docs/research/RESEARCH_topsides_dimensions_v1_2026-11-19.md
rules: Facts only, as R3's tables: which vent, where, how big, where it leads. No image or drawing of any plan is kept. Every row cites its source. Each row's tag is its clear area's: [read] where a source states it, [derived] where it is computed here from read numbers (R3's outlines, a printed diameter), [bet] where the plans are silent, each bet with its reason. A row's top carries its own tag (top_how).
reference: R3's tables of her rooms (data/rooms/<deck>_deck.json: Encyclopedia Titanica's free deck plans, read as tables of facts under docs/research/RESEARCH_rooms_plans_licence_v1_1_2026-11-20.md); The Shipbuilder, Midsummer 1911 special number, 'The White Star Liners Olympic and Titanic' (public domain), as B1+B2 quoted it from the topsides lane's OCR, its page numbers to a page; the topsides note (scaled heights off ET's plan and profile); The Shipbuilder's text read in the topsides lane's OCR (a text file kept outside the repository; the Olympic and Titanic number only: the file also holds the Mauretania's); the stern study's work as the coordinator digested it (STERNWORK digests 01_02 and 04_05, 2026-11-23, in the coordinator's notes folder): Wilding's evidence (BI 20391, 20392, 20921), Hendrickson's (BI 4912-4913), Faulkner 2001 and the FLOODSTAND doors; and Bob Read's hatches article and Mengot's casings, as the repository already cites them
how: A row is one way out for the air of one or more of the core's 64 spaces (space: its zone, sides P and S, and layer, 0 below E deck and 1 above): a machinery shaft to its skylight or funnel, a fan and its trunk, a hatch, a light and air trunk, a stair to the weather. Doors, windows and sidelights in her side (R3's data/rooms/openings.json, the core's C4) and S1's two grand staircases (the core's STAIRS) are the core's already and are not repeated here.
Place: by R3's rows (r3; the first is the one at its inlet), each row's outline clipped to the space's zone and sides; or by its frames (x).

Inlet: the deck it leaves its space at (deck). opens 'up': it leaves through its space's top (a shaft or hatch leaving a space below E deck at E deck); otherwise it stands on its deck inside its space.
Top: its outlet's height in the ship frame (z_top_m): a height read or scaled (top_z_m), or its top deck's height there, with the outlet's height over it (top_over_ft), each tagged in top_how.

Area: the narrower of its trunk (trunk_m2: the narrowest of the R3 rows above its inlet, each in the space's zone and sides, [derived]; or a fan's eye, the circle of its printed diameter, [derived from read], a lower bound on its shaft) and its way out (exit_m2, where read, derived or bet).
Hatches: their covers (hatch boards, tarpaulined where they meet the weather) are not read; each hatch row gives its clear opening, covered [bet]: NH7 takes it as a covered opening.

What closes it (closes) and at what head of water it gives way (gives_way: each with what gives way, the head or its range in metres where a source gives one, or when, the condition a source gives without a number, how, and a tag: the head's), where a source says. A cover lifted from below by air is a head of 0 to 0.1 m [bet unless read].
Derived fields (x_m, y_m, z_in_m, z_top_m, trunk_m2, exit_m2, area_m2, slab) are written by: node tools/vents_table.js --write

spaces_without.why: Her rooms over the reciprocating engine room (E to A decks): their ways out are S1's aft grand staircase and its dome (the core's STAIRS) and R3's windows, sidelights and doors (openings.json, the core's C4). The light and air trunks that pass them (R3 A-008: to the engine room and to the galley) belong to those spaces (V-001, V-008).

The third-class rooms under the poop (D and C decks, O to P): their ways out are R3's sidelights and doors to the poop deck (openings.json, the core's C4); no ventilator is read in R3's tables there, and No. 6 hatch is trunked through them (V-017).

The after peak, a tank under the steering gear: no air pipe or vent is read on the plans (R3's orlop row O-033 is the hold, not the tank's pipes). The Shipbuilder's account of the tanks was not read for it.

rows.check: The skylight's own outline and lights are not on ET's plan (it stands on the house's roof, z 30.53 m); the after dome beside it prints its panes, the skylight does not. rows.why: The skylight stands on the house's roof and is not drawn on ET's plan, so its lights are not found. notes.what: The central station (the electric engine room) is a separate watertight compartment about 63 ft long and 24 ft high, adjoining the turbine room's after end at the tank top (The Shipbuilder (1911), Olympic and Titanic number, about p. 107 [read]). Its own ventilation is not found: sealed [bet], no vent found. Its flat stands about 7.3 m (its 24 ft) over the tank top [derived]. V-009 to V-011 vent the stores and No. 4 hold above it, not it: for NH7 its air is nearly sealed [bet], a pocket under its flat.

Her accommodation (above E deck) was ventilated mechanically: 64 Sirocco fans of Davidson's, supply (a warm-air Plenum system to the passages and staterooms) and suction (from the lavatories, galleys and pantries), with no cowls to speak of (The Shipbuilder (1911), Olympic and Titanic number, about p. 106 [read]); and about 2,000 windows and sidelights. So above E deck her air leaves by her fan trunks (most of them not placed in R3's tables, rows here only where R3 reads a fan), her windows and sidelights (openings.json, the core's C4) and her staircases (S1).

The orlop over the shaft tunnels is a watertight flat (Wilding, BI 20392; the 1912 Report) [read, via the coordinator's digest of the stern study]: the tunnels' air is sealed under it but for the tunnels' own escapes [bet], a pocket for NH7.
As zone 13: the orlop over the shaft tunnel is a watertight flat (Wilding, BI 20392; the Report) [read, via the digest].
G deck over the after peak is a watertight flat (Wilding, BI 20392; the Report) [read, via the digest]: the after peak's air is sealed under it [bet], and no air pipe is read.

No deck was watertight but the weather deck, besides the flats named (Wilding, BI 20392) [read, via the digest]: the decks between the spaces leak; NH6 stage 1 opens a plate at its highest point for that.

The core's TOP connections (the weather deck open to the sea, a share fOpen, fitted) stand in for her hatches, companionways and doors (core.js, rebuildConnections) [read]: NH7 must not count those and this table's rows both (the stern study's caveat, via the digest).
